steps.message:
Use this layout so the central props file remains above the generated project:
```text
cpm-template/
|-- .template.config/
|   `-- template.json
|-- Directory.Packages.props
`-- src/
    `-- MyApp/
        `-- MyApp.csproj
```
`Directory.Packages.props`:
```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageVersion Include="Serilog" Version="4.2.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```
`src/MyApp/MyApp.csproj` keeps the reference versionless:
```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Serilog" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```
`.template.config/template.json`:
```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json.schemastore.org/template",
  "author": "Contoso",
  "classifications": ["Library"],
  "identity": "Contoso.Templates.CpmApp",
  "name": "Contoso CPM App",
  "shortName": "contoso-cpm",
  "sourceName": "MyApp",
  "tags": { "language": "C#", "type": "project" }
}
```
Package the whole `cpm-template` root. Keeping the props file at the generated repository root lets MSBuild find the matching `PackageVersion` for the versionless `PackageReference`.
